config.title: Counter App

intro.title: Counter App
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Counter App using React and TypeScript. You will learn how to manage state within a React component to track and update a numerical value. The core concepts include using the useState hook for state management and handling user events with onClick handlers. By the end, you will have a functional app that increments and decrements a counter displayed on the screen.
intro.usecase: The counter pattern is a foundational building block for interactive UI across countless real-world applications. You'll see it in e-commerce product quantity selectors, social media like/dislike buttons, and dashboard widgets that track metrics like unread messages or pending tasks. As a developer, implementing this pattern teaches you how to manage component state, handle user events, and update the UI reactively—skills essential for creating any dynamic interface, from a simple voting mechanism to complex inventory controls.

objectives: Initialize and manage component state using the useState hook
Implement event handlers to update state based on user interactions
Render dynamic content by binding state values to JSX elements
Configure button components with onClick event listeners
Construct a functional counter component with increment and decrement logic
Apply TypeScript type annotations to state variables for type safety
Manipulate state values through arithmetic operations within handlers

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports are added at the top of the file, making React and useState available for use.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement. You need to import both React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the Counter component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Counter that returns JSX. You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function.
steps.hint: Define a component that returns some JSX content, like a div with a heading.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the Counter component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A Counter component is defined and ready to be used.
successCriteria: A functional component named Counter is defined and returns JSX.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the Counter component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the component is named Counter and returns JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check that it's named Counter and returns JSX.

steps.title: Initialize counter state with TypeScript
steps.instruction: Inside your Counter component, initialize a state variable named 'count' using useState, typed as number with an initial value of 0.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. Remember to provide the type annotation for the state variable.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: typed state initialization
const [value, setValue] = useState<number>(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The Counter component will have a typed state variable 'count' initialized to 0, ready to be displayed and updated.
successCriteria: The component contains a useState call with type annotation <number> and initial value 0, storing the state in a variable named 'count'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with the type annotation <number> and initial value 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization is missing or incorrect. Use useState<number>(0) to create a typed state variable named 'count'.

steps.title: Define increment handler function
steps.instruction: Inside your Counter component, define a function named handleIncrement that increases the count state by 1.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls setCount with the updated value. You can use the current count value to calculate the new value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleIncrement function is defined inside the Counter component that increments the count state by 1 when called.
successCriteria: The handleIncrement function is defined and calls setCount with count + 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it properly updates the count state by calling setCount with count + 1.
steps.feedbackWrong: The increment handler function isn't defined correctly. Remember to create a function named handleIncrement that calls setCount to increase the count by 1.

steps.title: Add main container structure
steps.instruction: In the Counter component's return statement, replace 'null' with a div container that will hold the counter UI.
steps.hint: Return a JSX div element as the root container for your counter interface.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Counter component now returns a div container instead of null, providing a structure to hold the counter UI elements.
successCriteria: The Counter component returns a JSX div element
The return statement no longer returns null
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning a div element from the Counter component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Counter component should return a div container instead of null.

steps.title: Display the current count value
steps.instruction: Inside your Counter component's return statement, add a paragraph element that displays the current count value using JSX curly braces.
steps.hint:
Use the

tag and embed the count state variable inside curly braces to display its current value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a state value in JSX

Current value: {someState}
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show the current count value inside a paragraph element when the component renders.
successCriteria: A paragraph element exists in the return statement that displays the count state variable using JSX curly braces.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial:
You're close. Make sure you're using the

tag and embedding the count variable inside curly braces to display its value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph element displaying the count value is missing or incorrect. Check that you're using the correct JSX syntax.

steps.title: Add increment button with click handler
steps.instruction: Inside the Counter component's return statement, add a button element with the text 'Increment' and wire its onClick event to the handleIncrement function.
steps.hint: Place the button inside the div container. Use onClick={handleIncrement} to connect the click event to your handler function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The Counter component now includes a button labeled 'Increment' that, when clicked, will increase the count state by 1.
successCriteria: A button element with text 'Increment' is added inside the div container, and its onClick prop is set to handleIncrement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it has the correct text 'Increment' and the onClick prop is set to handleIncrement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The increment button is missing or not properly connected. Add a button with text 'Increment' and onClick={handleIncrement} inside the div.

steps.title: Add decrement and reset buttons with handlers
steps.instruction: Add two buttons inside the div after the increment button: one with text 'Decrement' that calls handleDecrement when clicked, and another with text 'Reset' that calls handleReset when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the onClick prop on each button to wire them to their respective handler functions.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will have three buttons: Increment, Decrement, and Reset, each wired to their respective handler functions.
successCriteria: Two new buttons are added: one with text 'Decrement' and onClick={handleDecrement}, and another with text 'Reset' and onClick={handleReset}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some buttons, but check that both buttons have the correct text and onClick handlers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons are missing or not correctly wired. Make sure to add both buttons with the specified text and onClick handlers.
